_comment: AD9 forecast settings. Priors are modelling assumptions, not data: change them and re-run. To point the pipeline at another district, change `district`.

state_env._note: spec 'sd4' = SD4's presidential+inflation+approval regression; 'mean' = presidential flag only (validates better, see output). Both refit on two-party shares. Inputs are [mean, sd].

lean._note: auto = lowest walk-forward MAE on the elections all methods can predict

p26: June 2026: county turnout vs June 2022 (Amador +5%, Calaveras +13%, Stanislaus +19%, SD4 data) applied to AD9's p22 35.0%; consistent with ~104,700 AD9 Assembly primary votes

incumbent._note: Flora's Assembly R share minus the top-of-ticket R share, in his district's precincts

primary_2026._note: Opt-in blend with the June 2026 Assembly primary (Democratic candidates' combined share). Needs Amador and Calaveras results to complete.
primary_2026._source: June 2026 AD9 Assembly primary: Adams 27,321 districtwide (26.1%, SOS); Perez 9,194 in Sacramento/San Joaquin/Stanislaus (SOS county pages) + ~660 estimated for the Amador/Calaveras parts (Perez:Adams ratio elsewhere); total ~104,700. Replace with certified districtwide totals.
primary_2026._shift_source: AD9 midterm top-of-ticket primary-to-general change: p14->g14 +1.3, p18->g18 -1.4, p22->g22 -2.5 pts

open_seat._note: Open-seat Assembly D share = top-of-ticket D share + N(edge_mean, candidate_quality_sd). Prior: no AD9-area D-vs-R open seat to calibrate.

primary_2028._note: Top-two primary, March 2028. Candidates' shares within each party ~ Dirichlet(concentration); lower = more lopsided fields.

votes._source: g22 AD9: 140,099 Assembly votes of 145,214 ballots; 2028 lower for a presidential ballot
